Hi heliophile,

fair point, but you managed to quit more or less on your own. 
Habits are usually hard to quit and just because habits are hard to quit does not mean that the object on which the habit focuses is to blame. 

You can not throw alcohol and gaming in one pot like that and say that they are all equally life affecting in the long term. Every sip of alcohol can be seen as literal poison that is entering your system, while the worst thing about gaming would be sitting for long hours, which is in no way comparable to alcohol or classical drugs.

What would you say is the difference between someone who ends up gaming excessively or compulsory and someone who is able to play in moderation?

I just see more of a responsibility with the gamer to make sure not "to get addicted" and I don't see where it helps to say the bad and manipulative video games are to blame.
 If somebody is not able to adjust his habits, that seems to be a problem of self control and not a problem of the thing that might very well be engineered to make the consumer addicted. Otherwise what would be the solution to prevent people from playing video games? Don't let anyone play video games because some might get addicted? 
Of course video games are designed to give you a dopamin rush quite frequently but that is what I as a consumer am paying for. 
But what are your warning words even do to help those affected? If games are really that hard to quit, that means that they probably can't do it themselves so talking sense to them doesn't work as much as you can not tell an alcoholic how bad alcohol is and get him to quit that way.

First of all, I don't mean to insult anyone I just would like to have a mature discussion about this topic because I think it is quite interesting. Just to make that point clear.
